name: Raycast
look: Four-step dark surface ladder, a white pill as the only bright element, hairline borders and no shadows anywhere.

hero.title: Your shortcut to everything
hero.sub: A launcher that replaces Spotlight, your clipboard history, your snippet manager and half the apps you open twice a day. One hotkey, everything behind it.

features.title: Everything behind one hotkey
features.sub: Built for people who would rather type four characters than move a mouse across two monitors.

items.title: Search everything
items.body: Applications, files, browser tabs, calendar events and every command from every installed extension, ranked by what you actually pick.

items.title: Clipboard history
items.body: Every copy, searchable, with images and formatting preserved.

items.title: Snippets
items.body: Expand boilerplate anywhere, with placeholders and dynamic dates.

items.title: Window management
items.body: Halves, thirds and displays from the keyboard.

items.title: Extensions
items.body: Nineteen hundred of them, written in React, installed in one keystroke.

items.title: Script commands
items.body: Wrap any shell script as a first-class command with arguments, so the thing you already automated becomes something you can actually find at the moment you need it.

showcases.title: Written in React, installed in a keystroke
showcases.body: Extensions are React components with a typed API for lists, forms, details and actions. There is no manifest to hand-write and no packaging step — write the component, run the dev command, and it is in your launcher.
points: Typed React API with hot reload

items.a: The launcher and every community extension are free forever, with no command limits and no advertising. Pro adds cloud sync, AI commands and themes for people who want them.
Everything except the AI commands and cloud sync runs entirely locally. Search indexes live on your machine and no query leaves it.

items.q: Can I write my own extensions?
items.a: Yes. Extensions are React components against a typed API. `beacon dev` gives hot reload against real data, and publishing is a single CLI command.
A Windows build is in beta. Linux is not currently on the roadmap, mostly because the window management layer would need rewriting per desktop environment.

cta.title: Press the hotkey
cta.sub: Free for macOS 13 and later. About nine megabytes, and no account needed to start.

footer.tagline: A launcher for people who would rather type than click.

notes: A four-step surface ladder does all the hierarchy: canvas → surface → elevated → card. There are no drop shadows anywhere in this system.
The white pill is the universal primary action. Everything else in the chrome is monochrome dark.
Hairline 1px borders carry every card edge — if an element needs to separate, it gets a border, not a shadow.
The radius vocabulary is deliberately multi-step: 6px keycaps, 8px buttons, 10px feature cards, 16px for the hero mockup container.
Saturated category accents belong inside extension tile imagery only, never on chrome. Putting one on a button breaks the system.
